lba_qa.q: A sweet shop has 120 chocolates and 90 candies. The owner wants to pack them into gift boxes so that each box has the same number of chocolates and the same number of candies, with no sweet left over. What is the maximum number of boxes he can make?
lba_qa.a:
We need the HCF of 120 and 90.
Prime factors: 120 = 2^3 x 3 x 5; 90 = 2 x 3^2 x 5.
HCF = 2 x 3 x 5 = 30.
So the maximum number of boxes = 30 (each box gets 4 chocolates and 3 candies).

lba_qa.q: Two bells in a temple ring at intervals of 18 minutes and 24 minutes. If they ring together at 6:00 AM, at what time will they next ring together?
lba_qa.a:
They ring together after a time equal to the LCM of 18 and 24.
18 = 2 x 3^2; 24 = 2^3 x 3.
LCM = 2^3 x 3^2 = 72 minutes.
72 minutes = 1 hour 12 minutes.
So they next ring together at 6:00 AM + 1 hr 12 min = 7:12 AM.

lba_qa.q: A shopkeeper says the product of the HCF and LCM of two numbers is equal to the product of the numbers. If two numbers are 15 and 20, verify this statement.
lba_qa.a:
HCF of 15 and 20: 15 = 3 x 5, 20 = 2^2 x 5, so HCF = 5.
LCM of 15 and 20 = 2^2 x 3 x 5 = 60.
HCF x LCM = 5 x 60 = 300.
Product of numbers = 15 x 20 = 300.
Both are equal (300 = 300), so the statement is verified.

lba_qa.q: A teacher wants to arrange 84 boys and 63 girls in rows so that each row has the same number of students and only boys or only girls in a row. Find the maximum number of students in each row.
lba_qa.a:
The maximum students per row = HCF of 84 and 63.
84 = 2^2 x 3 x 7; 63 = 3^2 x 7.
HCF = 3 x 7 = 21.
So each row can have a maximum of 21 students (4 rows of boys and 3 rows of girls).

lba_qa.q: Without doing long division, how can you tell that the number 7 x 11 x 13 + 13 is a composite number? Explain.
lba_qa.a:
Take 13 common: 7 x 11 x 13 + 13 = 13 x (7 x 11 + 1) = 13 x (77 + 1) = 13 x 78.
Since the number can be written as a product 13 x 78 (more than just 1 and itself), it has factors other than 1 and itself.
Therefore it is a composite number.

lba_qa.q: A gardener has 105 rose plants and 90 jasmine plants. He wants to plant them in rows with equal numbers and only one type per row. What is the largest number of plants he can put in each row, and how many rows in total?
lba_qa.a:
Largest plants per row = HCF of 105 and 90.
105 = 3 x 5 x 7; 90 = 2 x 3^2 x 5.
HCF = 3 x 5 = 15.
So 15 plants per row.
Rows of roses = 105/15 = 7; rows of jasmine = 90/15 = 6.
Total rows = 7 + 6 = 13.

lba_qa.q: Why is root 2 called an irrational number? Explain its meaning with a real-life link to measurement.
lba_qa.a: A rational number can be written as a fraction p/q (q not 0). Root 2 cannot be written as such an exact fraction — its decimal goes on forever without repeating. So it is called irrational. In real life, if a square has side 1 metre, its diagonal is root 2 metres, which cannot be measured exactly as a simple fraction — it is approximately 1.414... metres. This shows irrational numbers occur naturally in measurement.

lba_qa.q: Three runners take 12, 15 and 18 minutes respectively to complete one round of a circular track. If they start together, after how long will they meet again at the starting point?
lba_qa.a:
They meet again after a time equal to the LCM of 12, 15 and 18.
12 = 2^2 x 3; 15 = 3 x 5; 18 = 2 x 3^2.
LCM = 2^2 x 3^2 x 5 = 180 minutes = 3 hours.
So all three runners will meet again at the starting point after 180 minutes (3 hours).

lba_qa.q: A milk seller has 75 litres of cow milk and 45 litres of buffalo milk. He wants to fill them in cans of equal capacity such that each can has only one type of milk. Find the greatest capacity of such a can.
lba_qa.a:
Greatest can capacity = HCF of 75 and 45.
75 = 3 x 5^2; 45 = 3^2 x 5.
HCF = 3 x 5 = 15.
So the greatest capacity of each can is 15 litres (5 cans of cow milk and 3 cans of buffalo milk).

lba_qa.q: A number when written as a decimal terminates (ends), like 3/8 = 0.375. How can you tell, just by looking at the denominator, whether a fraction will give a terminating decimal?
lba_qa.a: A fraction in its simplest form gives a terminating decimal only if the denominator has prime factors of just 2 and/or 5 (no other prime factor). For example, 3/8: denominator 8 = 2^3, only the factor 2, so it terminates. But 1/3: denominator 3 has a prime factor other than 2 or 5, so it does not terminate (it repeats). This helps decide terminating vs non-terminating decimals without dividing.
lba_qa.topic: Rational numbers and their decimal expansions

Which of these numbers is irrational?

The fraction 3/8 gives a terminating decimal because the denominator 8 has only the prime factor:
lba_mcq.explanation: 8 = 2^3, only the prime factor 2. Denominators with only 2 and/or 5 give terminating decimals.

lba_mcq.q: A milk seller fills 75 L cow milk and 45 L buffalo milk into cans of equal greatest capacity (one type per can). The capacity of each can is:
Any composite number can be expressed as a product of:
lba_mcq.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, every composite number can be written as a unique product of prime numbers.
